name: Gbaya of Bossangoa / Gbeya
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source.
catalog_citation: Ruckstuhl, Christoph. 1998 [file version 2007]. Phonology of Gbaya of Bossangoa. Prepublication draft, Summer Institute of Linguistics, Central African Republic Branch. 57 pp. (SIL Language & Culture Archives resource 70786; PDF 'Phonology_Gbeya_Version_2007.…
catalog_locator: sec. 5.2 'Stress', p. 24 (with sec. 5.1, 5.3 on the same page); tone: sec. 7 'Tone', p. 26
catalog_quote: 5.1 Ambiguous Segments ... For representation and tone, long vowels are analyzed as two consecutive vowels for they represent two moras. For syllable patterns however, they count as one unit. 5.2 Stress Gbaya has no phonemic stress. It is therefore not analyzed here. 5.3 Intonation There are different intonation patterns for affirmative clauses, commands and questions. (cf. Samarin 66 p.31). They are not analyzed here. ... 7. TONE Gbaya has two phonemic tones. Utterance level intonation is used phonemically for questions and commands. There are two contrasting pitches, one high, one low (Samarin 66 § 113) (Montgolfier 75/3 p.5) and rise and fall only on long vowels. ... Tones are lexical, except for verbs and their derivations. Tones are grammatical on verbs, e.g. aspect, but predictable and redundant with their suffixes

tone_statements.citation: Ruckstuhl, Christoph. 2016. Proposition d'orthographe du Gbaya de Bossangoa (Gbeya) -- révisé [Orthography Proposal for Gbaya of Bossangoa (Gbeya)] (révisée après l'atelier de tonalité en 2015; researchers Beth Knapp, Paul Murrell). Draft manuscript, 23 pp. SIL Language & Culture Archives, entry 70979. SIL International.
tone_statements.quote: Les tons s’écriront comme en sango, si ce n’est que le gbaya ne comporte pas de ton moyen. Le ton bas est non marqué, le ton haut, avec un accent circonflexe sur la voyelle. Les voyelles longues seront aussi écrites sous la forme d’une séquence de voyelles, qui peuvent toutefois porter un ton différent. [...] [p. 6] Suite à l’analyse de ton de la langue gbeya qui a été effectuée pendant l’atelier sur la tonalité en janvier 2015 à Yaoundé, Cameroun, nous recommandons marquer le ton partiellement [...] La forme accomplie du verbe normalement porte la mélodie tonale Bas Haut (B.H). Mais si le complément d’objet direct qui suit le verbe porte le ton haut sur sa première syllabe, le verbe se prononce à ton bas.
tone_statements.translation: Tones will be written as in Sango, except that Gbaya has no mid tone. Low tone is unmarked; high tone is written with a circumflex on the vowel. Long vowels will also be written as a sequence of vowels, which may however carry different tones. [...] Following the tone analysis of the Gbeya language carried out during the tone workshop in January 2015 in Yaoundé, Cameroon, we recommend marking tone partially [...] The completive form of the verb normally carries the tonal melody Low High (L.H). But if the direct object following the verb has a high tone on its first syllable, the verb is pronounced with low tone.
tone_statements.locator: p. 2, section 'Compatibilité avec l'orthographe sango'; and p. 6, section 'Graphèmes tonals', a. 'La forme accomplie'
tone_statements.n_tones: 2 (H, L; explicitly no mid tone); verb melody L.H in the accompli

sources.note: States Gbeya has two tones, high and low, and unlike Sango no mid tone; low unmarked, high written with a circumflex; long vowels = vowel sequences that may carry different tones (p. 2). Section 'Graphèmes tonals' (pp. 6-9) reports the tone analysis done at the January 2015 tone workshop (Yaoundé) and recommends partial tone marking: subject pronouns change tone with the verb form (H in the affirmative accompli), the accompli verb carries a L.H melody but is realised L before an object with initial H, the negative accompli verb takes H as in the inaccompli, derived adjectives carry H, several…

In Moran, Steven & McCloy, Daniel (eds.), PHOIBLE 2.0. Jena: MPI-SHH. Online:https://phoible.org/inventories/view/720.Inventory digitised from Hartell, Rhonda L. (ed.) 1993, Alphabets des langues africaines (Dakar: UNESCO & SIL) via Chanard, C. 2006, Systemes alphabetiques des langues africaines (LLACAN online database, sumale.vjf.cnrs.fr/phono).

sources.note: The AA 720 inventory (45 segments) includes four tone units - high (˦), low (˨), falling high-low (˦˨) and rising low-high (˨˦) - alongside the consonant and vowel segments; no prose analysis, no TBU statement; secondhand from an alphabet/orthography source. Consistent with the two-level H/L system listed here (contours = sequences on long vowels per Ruckstuhl).

tone.n_tones: 4 tone units listed (H, L, HL, LH), i.e. two levels plus two contours
